failure_summary.description: Agents re-searched, selected a less-filtered result, or treated a category-scoped cache as covering a newly named entity instead of resolving the changed scope.
Agents treated a requested restaurant rating as an exact value, while the expected range treats it as a minimum threshold.
Agents omitted result assignment or caching, or saved an undefined result variable.
An agent omitted an active cuisine constraint and added an unsupported vegetarian preference.
An agent supplied a literal checkout date instead of deriving it from the explicit stay length with adjust_date.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers result assignment and saving, active-constraint retention, and deriving checkout dates, so repeating those rules is unlikely to help. These edits clarify two remaining ambiguities: which compatible cache entry to prefer (and when a category-scoped result cannot establish a newly named entity), and how to interpret requested numeric ratings.

edits.target: Choose a result whose domain, location, dates or leg, and original scope can cover the request: a broader candidate set may be filtered, but do not use a narrower result for a broader request.
edits.content: Choose the most constrained compatible cached result—prefer an entry that already embodies the greatest number of still-active criteria—while ensuring its domain, location, dates or leg, and original scope can cover the request. Retrieve that entry by its exact key, then apply only newly supplied filterable criteria; do not choose a broader base result when a compatible filtered result is available. A cache restricted to a different category or entity does not establish that a newly requested specific entity is included; search for that entity if the cached scope cannot cover it. Do not use a narrower result for a broader request.

edits.target: Distinguish hotel stars (`stars`) from guest ratings (`rating`); for a supported “at least N stars” constraint, use the inclusive range from N to the field's maximum, and for an exact category use the same value as both bounds.
edits.content: For restaurant ratings and hotel guest ratings, interpret a requested “N-star rating” or “N or higher” as a minimum threshold unless the user explicitly requests an exact rating; use the inclusive range `[N, 5]` in `rating`. Use `[N, N]` only for an explicitly exact rating.
